evidence.detail: runtests() extends args with find_files(arg, 'py') results; if argv is non-empty but no files match, args stays [] and pytest runs all tests
find_files() filters by needle in basename; 'parser_test' matches no tracked .py file, so returns []
subprocess.call(['pytest'] + []) with only -x/-m flags runs the full matching test suite, not an empty set

triage.fix_sketch: In dev.py:runtests(), after the loop that populates args from find_files(), add: 'if list(argv) and not args: sys.exit(f"No test files found matching: {list(argv)}")'. This makes the command fail with a clear message instead of silently running all tests when the needle matches nothing. Only dev.py needs to change.
triage.notes: The issue comment confirms the root cause: a bad search with no matches runs all tests. The fix is a 2-line guard.
